question: Which of the following is NOT a family in classification of Modern Indian Languages?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Indo - African.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indo-African** is not a recognized family in the classification of **Modern Indian Languages.**
 
• The other options are recognized **language families in India.**
 
• **Indo-European** refers to languages like **Hindi, Bengali, and Punjabi**, while Sino-Tibetan refers to languages like **Tibetan and Burmese.**
 
• **Dravidian** refers to a language family that includes languages like **Tamil, Telugu, and Kannada**, and is one of the major language families in India.
 
• It is important to note that the classification of languages into families is based on** linguistic similarities and differences,** and can change over time as new research is conducted.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The key word in the question is **"classification of Modern Indian Languages,"** which refers to the categorization of languages spoken in India based on **linguistic similarities and differences.**
 
• **Indo-European** is the largest language family in India, and includes many of the most widely spoken languages in the country.
 
 
• It is also spoken in many other parts of the world, including** Europe and parts of Asia.**
 
 
 
• **Sino-Tibetan** is a language family that is primarily spoken in** East Asia**, but also includes some languages spoken in India, like **Manipuri and Tibetan.**
 
• **Dravidian** is one of the major language families in India, and includes languages spoken primarily in** South India.**
 
 
• It is distinct from **Indo-European and Sino-Tibetan, **and has its own unique characteristics and features.
